deep.reconstruction:
Context (Ch. 14 of the Tractatus, E792). Euler studies quadratic residues for the moduli N = 2p+1 (N prime, implicitly) and 4N. A 'residue' means a quadratic residue among the numbers below the modulus that are prime to it.

Tables (continuing the examples of §516).
- N = 11. Residues are 1, 3, 9, 5, 4, i.e. the squares 1, 3^2, 3^4, ... and 2^2 = 4. Non-residues are 2, 6, 7, 8, 10.
- 4N = 44. Residues are 1, 9, 25, 5, 37: these are 1, 3^2, 5^2, 7^2 = 49 ≡ 5 and 9^2 = 81 ≡ 37. The 15 non-residues are arranged in three rows, each the residue row multiplied by 3, 7 and 13 respectively (mod 44):
  - 3·R = 3, 27, 31, 15, 23
  - 7·R = 7, 19, 43, 35, 39
  - 13·R = 13, 29, 17, 21, 41
- N = 13. Residues are 1, 3, 4, 9, 10, 12; non-residues are 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 11.
- 4N = 52. Residues are 1, 9, 25, 49, 29, 17, i.e. (2k+1)^2 mod 52 for k = 0..5. The 18 non-residues are the cosets 3R, 5R, 7R:
  - 3R = 3, 27, 23, 43, 35, 51
  - 5R = 5, 45, 21, 37, 41, 33
  - 7R = 7, 11, 19, 31, 47, 15

The implicit method (my reading) is that the non-residues fall into cosets c·R of the residue subgroup.

§517. Let R_N = {1, α, β, ...} and R_{4N} = {1, A, B, ...}; both sets have p elements. If A is in R_{4N}, then x^2 ≡ A (mod 4N) implies x^2 ≡ A (mod N). So A reduced mod N (by subtracting 0, N, 2N or 3N) lies in R_N.

§518. Every residue A mod 4N satisfies A ≡ 1 (mod 4). The reason: a unit x mod 4N is odd, so x^2 ≡ 1 (mod 4), and x^2 − (4q−1) ≡ 2 (mod 4) can never be a multiple of 4N. Hence 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, ... (when prime to N) are always non-residues.

§519. Suppose 4q+1 is in R_N, say a^2 ≡ 4q+1 (mod N). Then also (N ± a)^2 ≡ 4q+1 (mod N). One of a and N − a is odd; choose that one. Then a^2 ≡ 1 ≡ 4q+1 (mod 4). Since gcd(4, N) = 1, a^2 ≡ 4q+1 (mod 4N), so 4q+1 is in R_{4N}.

§520. If 4q−1 is in R_N, it is not in R_{4N} (by §518). But 2N + 4q − 1 = 4(p+q) + 1 is ≡ 1 (mod 4) and ≡ 4q−1 (mod N), so by the argument of §519 it is in R_{4N}.

§521. If 2q is in R_N, then 2q + N and 2q + 3N are both odd and differ by 2N ≡ 2 (mod 4). So exactly one of them is ≡ 1 (mod 4), and that one is in R_{4N}; the other, ≡ 3 (mod 4), is excluded.

§522. Case N = 4m+1 (p = 2m):
- If 4q is in R_N, then 4q + N ≡ 1 (mod 4), so it is in R_{4N}.
- If 4q+2 is in R_N, then 4q + 2 + 3N = 4q + 12m + 5 ≡ 1 (mod 4), so it is in R_{4N}.

§523. Case N = 4m−1 (p = 2m−1):
- If 4q is in R_N, then 4q + 3N = 4q + 12m − 3 ≡ 1 (mod 4), so it is in R_{4N}.
- If 4q+2 is in R_N, then 4q + 2 + N = 4q + 4m + 1 ≡ 1 (mod 4), so it is in R_{4N}.

Overall content (my summary). By CRT, R_{4N} = {A mod 4N : A ≡ 1 (mod 4), A mod N ∈ R_N}. Each residue mod N lifts to exactly one residue mod 4N, namely the unique lift among r, r+N, r+2N, r+3N that is ≡ 1 (mod 4). This gives the bijection R_N ↔ R_{4N} stated in §524 of the next page.
errors: No mathematical errors found. All four tables check (residue sets and the coset rows for 44 and 52 are exactly correct).

Implicit assumption (not stated on this page): 2p+1 is prime, needed for the count of p residues (§517 'multitudine aequalia') and for the coset structure of the tables; the lifting arguments of §§518-523 themselves only need 2p+1 odd.
Minor: §518's list 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23 should be restricted to numbers prime to the modulus (e.g. 15 is not a unit mod 4·5 or 4·3), though it is harmless for the prime N > 23 intended.

results.what: A unit A is a quadratic residue mod 4N (N odd) iff A ≡ 1 mod 4 and A is a QR mod N; explicit lifting rule: add 0, N, 2N or 3N to make the number ≡ 1 mod 4
results.modern_name: Structure of quadratic residues modulo composite moduli via Chinese remainder theorem (QR mod 2^k·m)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (Tractatus, c. 1750) / systematically Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae (1801) §§100-105

results.what: Non-residues mod 4N form cosets c·R of the residue group (tables for 44 and 52)
results.modern_name: Cosets of the subgroup of squares in (Z/nZ)^*
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (residue theory in E262/E449 and Tractatus)

results.what: Number of residues mod 4(2p+1) equals p, non-residues 3p

deep.surprise_reason: Routine elementary lifting of quadratic residues from modulus N to 4N; the Tractatus de numerorum doctrina is published (Commentationes arithmeticae, 1849) and well known as Euler's.

sorted([c*r % 44 for c in [3,7,13] for r in [1,9,25,5,37]]) == sorted([x for x in range(44) if gcd(x,44)==1 and x not in [1,5,9,25,37]])
checkable.asserts: Euler's three non-residue rows for 44 are exactly the 15 non-residues

sorted([c*r % 52 for c in [3,5,7] for r in [1,9,25,49,29,17]]) == sorted([x for x in range(52) if gcd(x,52)==1 and x not in [1,9,17,25,29,49]])
checkable.asserts: Euler's non-residue rows for 52 are exactly the 18 non-residues

checkable.asserts: Lifting rule of §524: each QR r mod N, shifted by kN to be ≡1 mod 4, is a QR mod 4N
